###### About Me
## Putting My Experience to Work
Alex Amoroso has dedicated his life to service—on the battlefield, in the classroom, and in the community. A U.S. Army officer, civic leader, and lifelong advocate for education, opportunity, and sustainability.
Military Service
U.S. Army Officer with deployments overseas, embodying honor, duty, and commitment.
Public Service
Worked at the federal, state, and local level to solve real problems and deliver results.
Community Engagement
Actively involved in programs that expand education access, protect the environment, and create career opportunities.
###### "Alex's leadership is rooted in values passed down through his family's tradition of military service and community involvement: chivalry, honor, and dedication to the greater good."
###### OUR PLATFORM
## Priorities for Mountain View
## Building a Mountain View that works for everyone—with smart policy, strong partnerships, and bold vision.
## 01
## Mountain View P3: Jobs & Career Pipeline
A bold plan to connect residents to good-paying jobs through partnerships between the city, businesses, and nonprofits. By leveraging infrastructure funds, job training, and even exploring universal basic income (UBI) pilots, we can ensure economic mobility and opportunity for all.
## 02
## Environmental Stewardship & Conservation
From preserving local parks to reducing our carbon footprint, Alex will champion sustainability through policies that protect natural resources, promote renewable energy, and keep Mountain View beautiful for future generations.
## 03
## Expanding Education Access
Education is the foundation of opportunity. Alex will fight for better access to high-quality learning, job retraining programs, and youth leadership development initiatives.
## 04
## Affordable Housing Through Public–Private Partnerships
Alex believes in creating affordable housing by working with local businesses and commercial developers —not relying solely on government-run projects. By streamlining processes and building smart partnerships, we can meet housing needs faster and more efficiently and in new and different ways such as with cohousing projects meeting sustainability requirements and workforce housing meeting the needs of the community and local economy.
## 05
## Community, Leadership, and Service
Alex believes in a connected city where residents feel heard and supported—whether that's improving public safety, expanding healthcare access, or building spaces where neighbors can come together.

links.text: I'l Portale - A constant on Moffett Boulevard

Alta Housing

Providing housing and services for low-income families, seniors, and people with disabilities. Supporting Alta Housing reflects a commitment to dignity, stability, and stronger communities

Housing Choices

Serving people with developmental, mental, and physical disabilities, including veterans and non-veterans, with housing and support services that promote independence, care, and inclusion.

Climate Action California

Climate Action California is an active community of individuals, organizations, and groups—working together to promote science-based climate solutions. We are engaged at every level of government—local, regional, state, and federal—advancing science-based climate policy that will speed the transition to a just, equitable low-carbon economy and a healthy planet. Our theory of change depends on strong, mutually respectful relationships with legislators and regulators, as we advocate for bold and effective action. New volunteers are always welcome to bring energy and new ideas to the work!

The Tamien Nation

The Native American tribe is ancestral to the Santa Clara Valley and San Francsico Bay Area. Specifically to Mountain View, they are indigenous to the Stevens Creek Trail territory. They provide not only insight on education about their people's history and preservation of culture, they also provide professional stewardship and that is both in line with the tribe's traditions and with modern government environmental policy. Alex is happy to work with this proud community so they have more opportunities for leadership and decision making in the community they were the first to establish.

Silicon Valley Chapter Military Officers Association of America

The primary mission of SVC MOAA is to support veterans and active-duty military members and their families. The organization will embrace diversity while leveraging varying skills to meet the needs of all veterans of Santa Clara County. The organization will make the necessary investments in personnel, systems, and processes for continued growth, organizational distinction, and community involvement.

The American Association of People with Disabilities

The American Association of People with Disabilities works to increase the political and economic power of people with disabilities. As a national disability-led and cross-disability rights organization, AAPD advocates for full civil rights for over 60 million Americans with disabilities. Alex is honored to work with and support their mission in promoting equal opportunity, economic power, independent living, and political participation for all veteran and non-veteran disabled Americans through AAPD.

The California Disability Leadership Alliance

Formed in 2024, the CDLA comprises several disability and Deaf-led organizations. The goal of the Alliance is to build cross-disability collaboration, solidarity, and political power to influence and improve policies for disabled people in California.

Canopy connects communities through thriving urban forests.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: Canopy prioritizes tree planting and stewardship, education, and advocacy in communities where people do not have a thriving urban forest due to limited resources, competing priorities, historical development, and urbanization patterns.

LifeMoves

Ten years ago, two organizations joined forces with a mission to address a challenging and seemingly impossible task—bring everyone home and build stronger communities.

LifeMoves is dedicated to helping individuals and families experiencing homelessness to return to stable housing and self-sufficiency.

UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County

The UC Master Gardener Program of Santa Clara County is a volunteer organization sponsored by the University of California Cooperative Extension. Our mission is to extend research-based knowledge and information on home horticulture, pest management, and sustainable landscape practices to county residents.
 
Our volunteers complete a 16-week, 60+ hour training program in home horticulture and remain certified on a yearly basis.

America's Gold Star Families

Providing Honor, Hope, and Healing for grieving military families who have lost a loved one while serving on active duty, regardless of military loss.

America’s Gold Star Families is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization created to assist those grieving any military loss through active duty service. We include all family members representing all conflicts, all branches of service, and all circumstances of death.

Blue Star Mothers of America, Inc.

Blue Star Mothers of America, Inc. is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting military service members, veterans, military families, and the families of our Fallen Heroes.

Founded in 1942, Blue Star Mothers brings together mothers, stepmothers, grandmothers, foster mothers, and female legal guardians who have children serving in the military, National Guard, or Reserves, as well as those whose children are veterans.

# Endorsements and Supporters
Alex Amoroso's campaign for City Council is powered by neighbors, veterans, small business owners, nonprofit leaders, and community members who believe Mountain View deserves practical leadership rooted in service, partnership, and results.
ENDORSE ALEX
ABOUT ALEX
###### —FEATURED ENDORSEMENT
# Endorsed by VoteVets
Alex is proud to be endorsed by VoteVets, a national organization supporting veterans, military families, and leaders committed to public service.
As a U.S. Army officer and public servant, Alex understands that leadership is not about titles — it is about showing up, taking responsibility, and serving something larger than yourself.
# Endorsed by AGAPE Silicon Valley
Agape Silicon Valley's work reflects the kind of community-centered leadership Alex believes in: supporting families, strengthening neighborhoods, and helping people access opportunity with dignity.
​
Agape Silicon Valley delivers food, water, supplies, and clothing to 20 different unhoused communities in Santa Clara and Alameda counties.
# Endorsed by Golden State - Property Management
Alex is proud to be endorsed by Golden State Property Management, a Silicon Valley company committed to treating property owners, tenants, and homes with dignity and respect.
Their focus on stewardship, compassionate care, and strong neighborhoods reflects the kind of community-centered leadership Alex will bring to City Council.
# Endorsed by BIA Bay Area
BIA Bay Area advocates for housing that meets the needs of people at all income levels, representing residential development professionals across the region.
Their focus on expanding housing opportunities aligns with Alex’s commitment to building strong neighborhoods where families can put down roots and thrive.
# Endorsed by Seamless Bay Area
Alex supports Seamless Bay Area’s vision for a unified, accessible, and equitable public transit system that better connects our communities.
Through the Bay Area Transportation Candidate Questionnaire, Alex shared his transportation priorities with voters, reinforcing his commitment to making it easier and safer for residents to get where they need to go.
###### —INDIVIDUAL ENDORSEMENTS
# Robert M. Henely
Monta Loma homeowner and Mountain View Kiwanian
Mountain View faces real challenges — affordable housing, public safety, and keeping opportunity within reach for working families — and meeting them will take steady, principled leadership.
I'm proud to support Alex Amoroso for City Council. A U.S. Army officer and dedicated public servant, Alex brings the discipline to listen, the integrity to follow through, and a genuine plan to connect residents with jobs and housing through real partnerships. As someone who has owned homes and been active in Mountain View's community and charitable life for years, I know the kind of neighbor this city needs on its Council. Alex is that neighbor. He has earned my endorsement.
# Richard Nguyen
Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, Mountain View Neighborhood Volunteer, US Army Veteran
Since 2019 I've seen his work ethic and how he strives to make his ideas a reality. He wants to protect the common man and the underprivileged against corporations and big businesses that take advantage of them.
He's both a lover AND a fighter who's willing to fight for everyone he cares about and is responsible for. I've seen how his drive, tenacity, and persistence make the lives of everyone around him and close to him. The people of Mountain View would be lucky to have him on the City Council.
# Michael Singleton
Blossom Valley Neighborhood Association, Mountain View Rotary Club, Mountain View Neighbor, US Navy Retired
Alex has a military background which is much needed in the City Council. He would bring organizational, leadership, and dedication to purpose to the office. Service above self is a much needed commodity in our government and that is what military service teaches.
# Todd Langton
executive Director, Agape Silicon Valley
When I first met Alex, I was immediately struck by his passion for serving others. His military service reflects a strong sense of selflessness, loyalty, and responsibility.
These qualities have shaped his approach to public service and his desire to contribute meaningfully to the Mountain View community.
# Diana Carbone
President 2026-2027 Los Altos Kiwanis Club
Alex is addressing some of the key problems we are facing in Silicon Valley. With his experience in both military and non-military government leadership, his collaboration among communities and industries, are all the kinds of leadership we want to see.
I fully support and endorse Alex as a candidate for Mountain View City Council.
# John Chu
Old Mountain View Neighborhood Association
In just fifteen minutes, Alex completely blew me away. It wasn't just that he possesses sensible plans, like using public-private partnerships to hold developers accountable while building workforce housing. It was his profound personal attributes: his exceptional clarity, his innate leadership, and his genuine willingness to engage with differing viewpoints. Alex didn't approach me with a rehearsed political script; he listened, processed, and showed a rare capacity for pragmatic problem-solving.
​
Mountain View does not need more ideological gridlock or spineless policy. We need forward-looking leadership that can bridge divides and execute smart solutions. Alex Amoroso has the character and the vision to do exactly that. He has my enthusiastic support in this upcoming election, and I urge my fellow residents to look past the toxic divisions and vote for him.
# Sanjay Dave
Mountain View Rotary, Former Mountain View School Board
# Nirvana Nwokidu
Mountain View Chamber of Commerce, Mountain View Satelite Rotary, Monta Loma Neighborhood Association
# Roger Dong-Neighbor
American Legion Program Analyst, Chinese American Heroes, US Army Retired
# Judy Hannemann
Mountain View Los Altos Union High School Board of Trustees, Mountain View Rotary Club

Alex is grateful for the support of Mountain View small businesses and neighborhood institutions that help make our city vibrant, welcoming, and economically strong.
